## What this letter says
An eye specialist wrote this letter to your eye doctor (optometrist). It is about your eye check.

- Your vision is 20/40 in the right eye. It is 20/50 in the left eye.
- Your eye pressure is 12 mmHg in both eyes.
- You have a dense 3 to 4+ nuclear sclerotic cataract in each eye.
- Your vision loss appears to be caused by the cataracts in both eyes.
- There is no relative afferent pupillary defect.
- The front of your eye (cornea) shows 1+ guttata in both eyes. This is mild.
- The mild guttata may mean early Fuchs dystrophy. This is possible, not certain.
- Your eye movements were intact. Your side vision was full in both eyes.
- The vitreous, macula, vessels and edges of the eye look normal. The cup-to-disc ratio is 0.1 in both eyes.
- The specialist says you should do well with cataract surgery.

## What you need to do
1. The specialist recommended cataract surgery. You agreed to have the first eye done.
2. The letter does not list other tasks for you.

## Dates and medicines
- Surgery on the first eye: "shortly". No date is given.
- The specialist will keep your eye doctor up to date. This will happen as surgery is done on each eye.
- The letter lists no medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my first eye surgery be?
- What do cataract and guttata mean for me?
- What does possible early Fuchs dystrophy mean?
- Will I hear about each result after the surgery?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
